evals.prompt: How do I search for files in Google Drive by name?
evals.expected_output: Use `GET /files?q=name contains 'SEARCH_TERM'` with the Drive API v3. The `q` parameter supports Google's native query language. Always include `fields` to limit response size, e.g., `fields=files(id,name,mimeType,modifiedTime)`.
expectations: mentions the GET /files endpoint
describes the `q` query parameter syntax
mentions the `fields` parameter

evals.prompt: How do I read the contents of a Google Doc through the governed connector?
evals.expected_output: Use `GET /files/{fileId}/export?mimeType=text/markdown` (or `text/plain`). Google-native files cannot use `alt=media` for download; they must be exported to a readable format first.
expectations: mentions the /export endpoint
specifies mimeType parameter
notes that alt=media does not work for Google-native files

evals.prompt: Can I permanently delete a file through the governed Google Drive connector?
evals.expected_output: No. Permanent deletion is not available through the governed connector. Files may be moved to trash (which is reversible), but hard deletion requires different token scopes.
expectations: correctly states permanent deletion is not available
mentions trash as a possible alternative

evals.prompt: What resource types does Google Drive declare for Kei policy?
evals.expected_output: Per ADR-028: folder (no parent) and file (parent: folder).
expectations: lists folder and file resource types
mentions parent types
references ADR-028

evals.prompt: How does credential management work for the Google Drive connector?
evals.expected_output: Kei supplies a Google OAuth access token (or service account token) at run time via kei-proxy connector invoke. The agent never reads or stores a token, secret, or API key.
expectations: states that Kei handles credentials
mentions OAuth access token
confirms agent never stores secrets

evals.prompt: The user says they haven't authorized Google Drive yet and offers to paste a service account JSON key for you to use. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: I do not accept the service account key. I explain they need to connect through Kei: an owner runs `kei connectors create --provider googledrive --workspace W` and follows the OAuth URL, or uses `--credential-ref` if the key already exists in the secret manager. If already connected but broken, use `kei connectors reconnect <id>`.
expectations: refuses to accept a raw service account key
mentions `kei connectors create`
mentions `kei connectors reconnect` as a repair option

evals.prompt: What is a Drive ID for the Kei Google Drive connector, and how do I find it?
evals.expected_output: A Drive ID is the optional drive_id field that scopes the Kei connector to one Google shared drive; kei-proxy supplies it as the drive scope on Drive calls. Blank means the connecting user's My Drive plus every shared drive they can access. Find it by opening the shared drive in Google Drive (left nav: Shared drives); the ID is the last URL segment of the drive's folders URL. Shared drive IDs start with 0A; ordinary folder IDs usually start with 1 and are not drive IDs.
expectations: states that drive_id scopes the connector to one shared drive
says blank means My Drive plus every shared drive the user can access
explains the ID is the last URL segment of the shared drive URL
notes shared drive IDs start with 0A while ordinary folder IDs usually start with 1

evals.prompt: I want to connect the Kei Google Drive connector to my personal files. My Drive URL is https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/my-drive. What do I enter for the Drive ID?
evals.expected_output: Leave the drive_id field blank. /u/0/my-drive is My Drive and has no Drive ID; a blank field covers the user's My Drive plus every shared drive they can access.
expectations: says to leave the field blank
explains that My Drive has no Drive ID

evals.prompt: Here is the URL of our team's shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/0AExampleSharedDrive01. What do I enter for the Drive ID field?
evals.expected_output: Enter 0AExampleSharedDrive01 — the last URL segment. Paste only the ID, not the URL; the field accepts only [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}. Note that /u/1/ is the Google account index in the browser: at OAuth consent pick the same account that can see the drive, or the connector can't see it.
expectations: gives 0AExampleSharedDrive01 as the value to enter
says to paste only the ID, not the URL
mentions picking the same Google account at OAuth consent that can see the drive
